title_en: Mei Zhifang, Li Zhuoming, Chang Jingshan, and Yu Zhilai — fraud, forgery of official documents, and forgery of seals
keywords_en: criminal; fraud; forging official documents; seals; first instance; second instance; intermediate people's court; high people's court; Hebei Province; natural person; foreign-invested enterprise; criminal law; elements of fraud crime; determination of crime of forging official documents and seals; appropriateness of sentencing; affirm the original judgment; standby letter of credit fraud; forging bank guarantee letter; cross-border financial fraud
full_text_en:
Mei Zhifang, Li Zhuoming, Chang Jingshan, and Yu Zhilai — case of fraud, forgery of official documents and seals

Defendant Mei Zhifang (FRANCISCO HUNG MOY), male, born November 15, 1949, American national, former Chairman of the Board of Yalian (Group) Co., Ltd., New York City, USA, residing at 38-29 214th Street, New York City, USA. Arrested on June 16, 1993.

Defense counsel: Feng Jiping, lawyer of Lantian Law Firm, Shijiazhuang City, Hebei Province.

Defense counsel: Zhang Jinlong, lawyer of Lantian Law Firm, Shijiazhuang City, Hebei Province.

Defendant Li Zhuoming (RAYMOND C. LEE), male, born May 18, 1950, American national, former Secretary and Financial Controller of Yalian (Group) Co., Ltd., New York City, USA, residing at 8 Chatham Road, Gaomei District, New York State, USA. Arrested on June 16, 1993.

Defense counsel: Zhang Jinghe, lawyer of Xinhua Law Firm, Shijiazhuang City.

Defense counsel: Lyu Zhansuo, lawyer of Zhengda Law Firm, Shijiazhuang City.

Defendant Chang Jingshan, male, born May 29, 1939, former Deputy General Manager and Business Manager of the Trade Department of Hainan Zhongshui Great Wall International Investment Group. Arrested on July 27, 1993.

Defendant Yu Zhilai, male, born April 5, 1944, former person in charge of the Tianjin Office of Hainan Huafeng Trade Company. Arrested on July 27, 1993.

The Hengshui Prefecture Branch of Hebei Provincial People's Procuratorate filed a public prosecution with the Hengshui Prefecture Intermediate People's Court, charging defendants Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming with fraud and forgery of official documents and seals; defendant Chang Jingshan with forgery of official documents and seals; and defendant Yu Zhilai with forgery of official documents.

Upon trial, the Hengshui Prefecture Intermediate People's Court found the following facts:

Defendants Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming, introduced by an intermediary, arrived in Hengshui City, Hebei Province at the end of March 1993. Under the guise of "attracting investment", they submitted to Zhao Jinrong, President of Hengshui Central Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China (hereinafter "Hengshui ABC"), and Xu Zhiguo, Vice President, a false "investment attraction" commitment letter and a fabricated introduction of Yalian (Group) Co., Ltd., New York City, USA (hereinafter "Yalian"), falsely claiming that Yalian had strong financial strength and could "introduce huge funds" for Hengshui ABC on the international financial market, that Hengshui ABC only needed to issue a standby letter of credit as a necessary procedure for attracting investment without bearing any economic or legal liability, and that the introduced funds would not require repayment of principal or payment of interest, thereby deceiving Zhao Jinrong and Xu Zhiguo into trusting them. To conceal the true nature of their fraud, when Li Zhuoming translated the English text of the standby letters of credit into Chinese and submitted it to Zhao Jinrong and Xu Zhiguo for review, he deliberately omitted the translation of a passage in the English text stating that "the amount of the draft drawn represents debt related to the loan financing provided to Yalian (Group) Company", resulting in Zhao Jinrong and Xu Zhiguo issuing, on April 5, 1993, 200 irrevocable, transferable standby letters of credit with a total amount of USD 10 billion, with Yalian as the applicant, Hengshui ABC as the issuing bank, and Shawude Investment (Bahamas) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Shawude") as the beneficiary, valid for one year. On April 6, Li Zhuoming, following the address provided by Mei Zhifang, sent the aforementioned standby letters of credit to RMCIVOR (Canadian), the Financial Controller of Shawude. Subsequently, Mei Zhifang used the said standby letters of credit as collateral for a loan from Shawude. Thereafter, two foreign enterprises inquired with Hengshui ABC about the authenticity of the standby letters of credit it had issued. Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming again deceived Zhao Jinrong and Xu Zhiguo by claiming that Hengshui ABC faced no risk and that funds would soon be introduced, leading Hengshui ABC to provide unconditional confirmation of the issued standby letters of credit. On April 18, Zhao Jinrong, pursuant to the promises made by Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming, requested a counter-guarantee from Yalian for the standby letters of credit issued by Hengshui ABC. Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming forged a USD 10 billion standby letter of credit from United National Republic Bank and submitted it to Zhao Jinrong, continuing the deception. In June of the same year, RMCIVOR attempted to sell the standby letters of credit issued by Hengshui ABC in the United Kingdom and Switzerland. Due to relevant measures taken by authorities in China, no payments under the said standby letters of credit occurred within their validity period.

In March 1993, defendant Mei Zhifang was in Guangzhou to confirm forged standby letters of credit No. 0014 and No. 0015 of Sanya Branch of Agricultural Bank of China, totaling USD 1.68 billion, for Robert Pam of Canada. At the suggestion of defendant Chang Jingshan, and with the agreement of Mei Zhifang and defendant Li Zhuoming, Chang Jingshan arranged for someone to privately engrave the seals of Hebei Branch of Agricultural Bank of China and other entities. Subsequently, Mei Zhifang, Li Zhuoming, Chang Jingshan, and defendant Yu Zhilai jointly forged guarantee letters from Hebei Branch of Agricultural Bank of China for standby letters of credit No. 0014 and No. 0015. In April of the same year, Mei Zhifang, Li Zhuoming, Chang Jingshan, and Yu Zhilai again forged in Hengshui City a guarantee letter from Hebei Branch of Agricultural Bank of China for standby letter of credit No. 0015 in the amount of USD 1.6 billion. Both forged guarantee letters were sent by Mei Zhifang to Robert Pam.

The above facts are sufficiently confirmed by seized documentary evidence including the Yalian Group introduction, cooperation agreement for introducing foreign investment and development, letter of credit application, commitment letter, the original standby letters of credit issued by Hengshui ABC recovered from abroad, the USD 10 billion standby letter of credit issued by Mei Zhifang in the name of United National Republic Bank, the loan agreement and investment agreement between Shawude and Yalian, and by the criminal forensic technical identification of the forged guarantee letters by the public security authorities and witness testimony.

The Hengshui Prefecture Intermediate People's Court held that defendants Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming, with the intent of illegal possession, used methods of fabricating facts and concealing the truth to defraud the People's Republic of China of a huge amount of property, namely USD 10 billion, and their conduct constituted the crime of fraud as provided for in Article 152 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. The circumstances of the crimes of the said two defendants were particularly serious, and they should be severely punished according to law. Li Zhuoming, after the case came to light, could truthfully confess the criminal facts and expose some of the crimes of his accomplices, so a lighter punishment could be imposed at discretion. Pursuant to Article 30 of the Criminal Law, the additional punishment of deportation may be applied to foreigners who commit crimes. Defendants Mei Zhifang, Li Zhuoming, and Chang Jingshan jointly forged the seals of Hebei Branch of Agricultural Bank of China and other entities and forged guarantee letters for the relevant letters of credit, and their conduct constituted the crime of forgery of official documents and seals as provided for in Article 167 of the Criminal Law. Defendant Yu Zhilai participated in the forgery of guarantee letters of Agricultural Bank of China for the relevant letters of credit, and his conduct constituted the crime of forgery of official documents as provided for in Article 167 of the Criminal Law. Mei Zhifang and Li Zhuoming each committed multiple crimes, and pursuant to Article 64, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Law, they should be subject to cumulative punishment for multiple crimes. For criminals who seriously undermine social order, pursuant to Article 52 of the Criminal Law, the additional punishment of deprivation of political rights may be applied. Pursuant to Article 60 of the Criminal Law, the illegal gains of the criminals and their own property used for the crimes shall be confiscated.

Accordingly, the Hengshui Prefecture Intermediate People's Court, on April 25, 1994, rendered the following judgment:

1. Defendant Mei Zhifang was sentenced to fifteen years of fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of fraud, with the additional punishment of deportation and confiscation of USD 2,000 and one gold necklace; and to seven years of fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of forgery of official documents and seals; and was ordered to serve a combined sentence of twenty years of fixed-term imprisonment, deportation, and confiscation of USD 2,000 and one gold necklace.

2. Defendant Li Zhuoming was sentenced to ten years of fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of fraud, with the additional punishment of deportation; and to six years of fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of forgery of official documents and seals; and was ordered to serve a combined sentence of fourteen years of fixed-term imprisonment and deportation.

3. Defendant Chang Jingshan was sentenced to seven years of fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of forgery of official documents and seals, and deprivation of political rights for two years.

4. Defendant Yu Zhilai was sentenced to two years of fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of forgery of official documents.

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, defendants Mei Zhifang, Li Zhuoming, and Chang Jingshan refused to accept the judgment and filed an appeal. Mei Zhifang's grounds of appeal were: the USD 10 billion standby letters of credit, although sent abroad, were not cashed; his role in the forgery of official documents and seals was unimportant; and the original sentence was too heavy. Li Zhuoming's grounds of appeal were: he did not play a major role in the fraud crime and requested a lighter sentence. Chang Jingshan's grounds of appeal were: he voluntarily confessed to the crimes of forgery of official documents and seals and requested a lighter sentence.

Upon trial, the Hebei High People's Court held that: appellant Mei Zhifang planned the fraud against Hengshui ABC, which had already caused serious harmful consequences, and played a decisive role in the criminal activities of forging official documents and seals; appellant Li Zhuoming actively participated in the fraud against Hengshui ABC and played an important role in the criminal activities; appellant Chang Jingshan did not demonstrate voluntary confession of his crimes. The grounds of appeal of all three appellants were untenable. The facts of each defendant's crime as determined in the first instance judgment were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, the conviction was accurate, the sentence was appropriate, and the trial procedure was lawful. Accordingly, the Hebei High People's Court, pursuant to Article 136, item (1), of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered a final ruling on May 13, 1994, dismissing the appeals of appellants Mei Zhifang, Li Zhuoming, and Chang Jingshan and affirming the original judgment.
